sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球海事商船注册旗国、借鉴特拉华州公司法的非公开发行实体

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Distribution of Certified Civil Aircraft Rotables and Avionics Surplus

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid: statutory corporate law modeled on the United States common law tradition, with the Constitution and recognized customary law
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Compact of Free Association with the United States of America (2003, as amended)
No comprehensive bilateral investment treaty or double taxation agreement currently in force

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Business Corporations Act (Marshall Islands Revised Code Title 29, as amended); Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism Act 2012, as amended; AML/CFT Regulations and practice directives issued by the Registrar of Corporations and the Financial Intelligence Unit; beneficial ownership record-keeping obligations under MIRC Title 29 and the AML/CFT Rules.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certified copy of passport or national ID for each proposed director, shareholder, and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport or national identification authority in each origin country

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized source-of-wealth and source-of-funds declaration of each UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed bank or regulated financial institution and notary public in the jurisdiction of execution

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized subscriber resolution / power of attorney appointing the licensed registered agent and declaring authorized share subscriptions
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the jurisdiction of execution

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation and good standing of any corporate shareholder or UBO entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry in the entity's jurisdiction of incorporation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of all proposed directors, shareholders, UBOs, officers, and signatories against the Marshall Islands FIU domestic list, UN Consolidated Sanctions List, US OFAC SDN List, UK HMT sanctions list, and EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List. PEPs trigger enhanced due diligence, independent compliance approval, source-of-funds documentation, and escalation to the registered agent's Money Laundering Compliance Officer. Any sanctions match is reported to the Financial Intelligence Unit without tipping off.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: RMI Registrar of Corporations corporate registry (online name-clearance and entity filing portal; accessible via licensed Marshall Islands registered agents)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names are submitted in Latin script using English. Foreign-language transliterations are accepted only where the Registrar determines that the romanization is phonetically equivalent, is not misleadingly similar to an existing registered name, and includes no diacritics unsupported by the registry system.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If a name is rejected, the applicant has 14 calendar days from the notice date to file a written appeal with the Registrar accompanied by the original rejection notice, evidence of prior use or regulatory consent, and the prescribed appeal fee. The Registrar issues a written decision within 15 working days. If the appeal is denied, the applicant may submit a new name; if the new name is also rejected, the applicant may seek judicial review in the High Court of the Marshall Islands.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Yes. The company may have no physical premises in the Marshall Islands; a licensed registered agent's office in Majuro must be designated as the registered office and shall accept service of process. Virtual office arrangements are permitted only if the licensed agent maintains physical corporate records and a physical address at its registered office, and if the company maintains no unauthorized trade presence in the Marshall Islands.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate for this industry: approximately 5% baseline annual probability of an unannounced Registrar/FIU inspection, increasing to 10-15% where trigger events exist, including PEP involvement, sanctions list rounding, inconsistent source-of-funds data, or failure to update UBO records.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate name clearance and reservation fee (one-time, up to 120 days)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registrar of Corporations (collected by licensed agent)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Government incorporation filing fee for a standard Business Corporation (non-resident, no minimum capital)
Registered agent and registered office service fee (first calendar year)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for RMI corporate services

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO identification, PEP screening, and EDD compliance package
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market rate for enhanced due diligence under AML/CFT Act 2012

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and apostille/consular legalization of documentary bundle
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public and foreign ministry/competent authority
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official legalization and notary tariff schedules

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Marshall Islands Business Corporations Act (BCA), Title 11, Chapter 5 of the Revised Statutes of the Marshall Islands; principal provisions: Sections 9 (Articles of Incorporation), 13 (Filing and Recording), 20 (Registered Office and Registered Agent), 24 (Directors), 37 (Capital Shares), and 58 (Corporate Powers).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Office of the Attorney General, Majuro, Republic of the Marshall Islands
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form RA/BC-2) submitted to the Registrar of Corporations, accompanied by the registered agent consent and the applicable fee schedule
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a non-resident business corporation. Shares may be issued for any lawful consideration determined by the board; if par-value shares are issued, the aggregate par value must be paid in full before issuance. No escrow account is required by RMI law for incorporation, although a corporate escrow account may be adopted voluntarily to support aviation transaction security.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscription for 1,000 shares of no-par value Common Stock is approved, the shares are issued fully paid and non-assessable, and the subscriber's $1,000 contribution is deposited into the corporate account. RESOLVED, that the registered office is the office of the licensed registered agent in Majuro, Marshall Islands, and that agent is appointed. RESOLVED, that the following individuals are appointed officers: President, Secretary, and Treasurer, each to serve until successors are elected. RESOLVED, that the Secretary is authorized to file the Articles of Incorporation, pay all fees, and obtain the Certificate of Incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Office of the Attorney General, Majuro (submission through a licensed RMI registered agent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a Name Clearance Request to the Registrar through a licensed registered agent. Confirm the proposed name is distinguishable from registered business corporations, limited partnerships, and other entities and does not contain restricted terms such as 'Bank', 'Trust', 'Insurance', or 'Cooperative' unless separately licensed. Upon approval, the name may be reserved for a maximum 90-day statutory period.
required_dossiers: Corporate Identity Statement showing ISIC 4659 trading scope
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is queried for similarity or restricted language, respond with evidence of distinguishability or submit a revised name election within 5 business days to preserve the filing timeline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Engaging RMI Registered Agent and Establishing Registered Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered Agent licensed under the Marshall Islands Business Corporations Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the registered agency agreement and complete the Registered Agent Consent form, providing proof of the agent's RMI license and consent to act. The registered office must be a physical street address in Majuro and may not be a post-office box.
required_dossiers: AML/KYC Identity Pack of Beneficial Owner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registered agent or office is disqualified or ceases to act, appoint a substitute agent and file a Notice of Change of Registered Office and Registered Agent with the Registrar within 10 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft, Notarize, and Sign Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate counsel or notary acting for the incorporator/share subscriber
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation in accordance with BCA Section 9, including the corporate name, registered agent and office, purpose covering wholesale distribution and import/export of certified civil aircraft rotables, avionics, and surplus parts, and the authorized share structure. Execute the articles before a notary public or equivalent officer and adopt initial bylaws effective upon incorporation.
required_dossiers: Consent to Serve as Registered Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar's pre-filing review identifies defective or impermissible clauses, cure by filing a Certificate of Correction or expressly amended executed articles, paying only the prescribed correction fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Articles and Pay Registration Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Office of the Attorney General (electronic filing portal or counter window)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the executed Articles of Incorporation together with the state fee schedule computed on the authorized share capital. Wire or pay through the state-approved portal the official filing fee, and the Registrar will examine the documents for compliance with the BCA before issuing a certificate or requesting correction.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a deficiency letter is issued, cure the deficiency within 14 days by amending the offending provision and resubmitting; if the name reservation lapses during correction, re-reserve the name before re-filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certificate of Incorporation, Organizational Meeting, and Initial Governance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors and Corporate Secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Receive the Certificate of Incorporation and convene the first board meeting, or obtain unanimous written consent in lieu of meeting. Ratify the bylaws, appoint the initial officers, authorize issuance of share certificates, adopt the corporate seal and banking resolutions, and confirm the registered office records location.
required_dossiers: First Board Meeting Minutes or Unanimous Written Consent
Banking Resolution Authorizing SWIFT and Escrow Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a third-party financial institution questions corporate existence, obtain a Certificate of Good Standing or certified extract from the Registrar and provide the related governance resolutions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Trade License and Aviation Spares Distribution Authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Trade and Investment Division, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Employment, Republic of the Marshall Islands
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, apply for the commercial distribution license for aircraft spare parts and avionics under ISIC 4659. Submit the certificate of incorporation, environmental determination if applicable, and evidence of AML procedures for aviation escrow and SWIFT payment rails. Confirm that only certified airworthy components and certified surplus aircraft parts will be supplied.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and Good Standing
AML/Compliance Program Description for Aviation Payments
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the license is deferred after examination, rectify the cited deficiencies and resubmit; an appeal may be made to the Trade and Investment Division within 20 days of the adverse determination.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Trade and Investment Division, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Employment, Republic of the Marshall Islands, with aviation-specific oversight by the regulatory civil aviation authority where applicable
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Commercial Distribution License for Civil Aircraft Rotables, Avionics, and Surplus Aircraft Parts (ISIC 4659 Category)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority (EPA), Republic of the Marshall Islands
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B — EIA Registration for low-impact warehousing and distribution activities; no full EIA report required unless operations include stripping, chemical treatment, or open storage of hazardous aircraft residues
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater discharge; stormwater runoff from storage areas must comply with EPA water quality standards. VOC emissions from stored solvents and avionics cleaning agents must remain below the occupational workplace limit and the applicable EPA air strip standard. Waste contaminated aircraft parts, lubricants, or batteries must be segregated and transported under EPA hazardous waste handling schedule.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate from the Majuro Fire Department covering warehouse sprinkler, alarm, and evacuation compliance; structural load inspection certificate for racking and heavy cargo storage areas; and an occupational workplace clearance confirming first-aid provisions, emergency exits, hazardous spill kits, and fire extinguisher placement.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Commissioner of Revenue, Ministry of Finance, Republic of the Marshall Islands; customs matters administered by RMI Customs Service. No dedicated national taxpayer web portal exists for general tax registration; filings are lodged with the Ministry of Finance in Majuro.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities are not required to obtain a TIN or VAT ID solely for registration of a non-resident Business Corporation. The sole administrative requirement is incorporation with the RMI Registrar of Business Transactions and payment of the applicable annual franchise fee. If a non-resident BC later establishes a taxable nexus inside the Marshall Islands (e.g., derives RMI-source income or employs local staff), it must then apply to the Commissioner of Revenue for an RMI taxpayer identification number. No indirect-tax registration is available because the RMI levies no VAT, GST, or sales tax.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The RMI has no check-the-box, hybrid entity, or pass-through election under domestic tax law. A non-resident Business Corporation is taxed per se only on income derived from sources within the Marshall Islands; no entity classification election is available. Anti-hybrid mismatch adjustments of foreign jurisdictions do not create domestic RMI tax elections.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: None – the Republic of the Marshall Islands does not impose a VAT, GST, or general sales/use tax. Import and excise duties may apply at the border under RMI Customs legislation.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: N/A — no turnover-based indirect tax registration threshold exists. The RMI uses the United States Dollar (USD) as its official currency; the concept of a monetary threshold does not apply because no indirect tax is imposed.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No electronic invoicing, real-time fiscal clearance, API digital stamping, or government-approved e-invoicing mandate exists in the Marshall Islands. RMI Customs uses an electronic customs declaration system (ASYCUDA World) for import/export clearance, but this does not impose a continuous VAT clearance or invoice-submission obligation.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable in the direct sense: the Marshall Islands has no VAT/GST regime, so there is no zero-rating or export VAT refund mechanism. For customs duty purposes, qualifying exports (including surplus commercial aircraft parts and avionics) are outside the charge to duty when the goods are physically exported within the time limit prescribed by RMI Customs, the export declaration is duly completed, and no diversion, re-importation, or fraudulent misdescription occurs. Offshore services supplied by a non-resident BC are not subject to any RMI indirect tax.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (lodged with RMI Customs)
Bill of Lading or Master Air Waybill
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank transfer evidence (where export proceeds are repatriated)
Certificate of Non-Resident Business Corporation Status (if claiming exemption)
Export Permit or license (if required for controlled aviation goods)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: No VAT or indirect-tax clawback exists because the RMI imposes no VAT/GST. However, fraudulent claims for duty exemption or false export declarations are subject to RMI Customs Act enforcement, including revocation of the exemption, recovery of unpaid duties, monetary penalties (typically up to 200% of the duty evaded), seizure and forfeiture of the goods, and criminal prosecution. For payment flows, anti-money laundering and sanctions scrutiny may apply to cross-border aviation escrow and SWIFT wire transactions.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Republic of the Marshall Islands: no domestic central bank or statutory foreign-exchange administration exists. The U.S. dollar is sole legal tender under the Compact of Free Association, and monetary conditions are de facto set by the U.S. Federal Reserve System. In-jurisdiction banking supervision, AML/CFT oversight, and bank licensing rest with the Marshall Islands Banking Commission (Office of the Banking Commissioner, Ministry of Finance), supported by the Marshall Islands Financial Intelligence Unit as the national reporting center.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility on both current and capital accounts. The RMI imposes no exchange-control regime, no capital-account licensing, no inward-investment restrictions, and no statutory limitation on profit or dividend remittance for a non-resident Business Corporation in tax-exempt status. Practically, remittance friction derives from non-statutory layers: U.S. Treasury/OFAC sanctions screening at U.S. correspondent banks, enhanced due diligence triggered by offshore incorporation, and certification requirements such as IRS Form W-8BEN-E or equivalent U.S. beneficial-owner tax forms to avoid 30% U.S. withholding on U.S.-sourced payments. Once good-standing, beneficial-ownership, W-8, and source-of-funds evidence is complete, profit and capital remittance are effectively frictionless.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender obligation, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no repatriation timeline apply to export receipts under RMI law. Export proceeds from certified civil aircraft rotables and avionics surplus may be retained in USD in-country or abroad, or converted into any freely convertible currency. The operative constraints are documentary and correspondent-bank driven: wires must be supported by sales contract, commercial invoice, airway bill, ECCN/EAR99 classification note, and end-user undertaking; cash transactions at U.S. correspondents reaching USD 10,000 trigger Bank Secrecy Act currency-transaction reporting, so all proceeds must move by SWIFT wire rather than cash.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational USD demand deposit account with sub-account capability for aviation trade settlement
Capital escrow and development-collateral account; not positioned for commercial trading flows

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of Guam (Pacific regional commercial bank)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational USD account with aviation escrow and SWIFT wire capabilities

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of Hawaii (Pacific Desk, U.S. Federal Reserve member bank)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational USD account for offshore non-resident entities with treasury and correspondent capabilities

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium. Regulated offshore digital EMIs generally require applicant tax residence, director nexus, or a bank reference in a supported jurisdiction (US, UK, EU, SG, HK, or AU); an RMI non-resident Business Corporation with registered-agent premises but no local economic substance will usually fail automated EMI onboarding and be declined at sanctions and mother-list review. Because the RMI issues no e-money license, an EMI cannot act as the primary clearing bank. A limited viable use exists for small pre-funded operational disbursements after full counterparty screening, provided the EMI supports B2B trade purpose codes and transmits a transfer message compatible with U.S. correspondent OFAC screening.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Hybrid mandate. Domestic RMI banks effectively require at least one director or a duly appointed officer to appear physically at the Majuro branch for the initial KYC interview; there is no statutory exemption for non-resident BCs. Regional U.S.-chartered banks permit remote or video-based opening where all signatories complete a live liveness-verified interview, corporate documents are notarized and apostilled, passports are certified by an RMI notary or consular officer, and the registered agent supplies a physical-nexus letter. Fully automated no-interview onboarding is not available; biometric video verification is the minimum acceptable standard.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial ownership opacity: nominee shareholders, trust or foundation layers, or incomplete citizenship and tax-residence disclosure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sworn schedule of ultimate natural-person beneficial owners including full legal name, DOB, nationality, country of tax residence, and TIN; continuous beneficial-ownership filing with the RMI Registrar and Banking Commission; apostilled corporate charter; certified shareholder register; and an organizational chart tracing every intermediate entity to the natural person.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore shell profile: zero RMI employees, no physical office, registered-agent address only, and first-time banking relationship.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: RMI registered-agent agreement and physical-nexus letter; tax-exempt certification from RMI Treasury; current good-standing certificate; annual return filing receipt; board resolution appointing the treasury manager; D&O and general liability insurance certificates; and a bank reference from the shareholder's existing deposit institution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Industry red flag: aviation surplus parts distribution perceived as dual-use, ITAR/EAR-controlled, or exposed to counterfeit and unairworthy rotables.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: ECCN determination memorandum and EAR99 certification for each part class; OFAC SDN, Denied-Persons, and Unverified-List screening reports for all counterparties; FAA Form 8130-3 and EASA Form 1 airworthiness certificates or OEM release certificates; end-user and end-use undertakings from airlines and MRO customers; and third-party inspection reports evidencing traceable surplus origin.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value and high-frequency USD wires to non-bank counterparties or into jurisdictions under enhanced monitoring, triggering correspondent de-risking.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Transaction-profile questionnaire declaring counterparties, value bands, expected frequency, and settlement calendar; Escrow_Aviation rail instruction-flow diagram; commercial purchase and resale contracts establishing genuine trade; vendor onboarding file for each supplier; no-cash and no-crypto undertaking; and the RMI tax-exempt status certificate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital escrow or shareholder-loan injection from a third party not clearly registered as a subscriber of the Business Corporation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed subscription agreement or shareholder-loan instrument; source-of-wealth letter from the funding bank; board resolution approving the injection; no-clawback undertaking; and a SWIFT-message reference protocol requiring the escrow ID and invoice number in the remittance information field for straight-through reconciliation.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital follows four compliance steps: (1) board resolution, with any required filing to the RMI Registrar, authorizing the capital injection; (2) remittance exclusively from the named shareholder's own regulated bank account via SWIFT MT103 benefitting the MH_BC operational or escrow account, with narrative stating 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION - NON-RESIDENT BUSINESS CORPORATION' and an escrow or subscription reference for reconciliation; (3) sender confirmation as a licensed financial institution, with no cash deposits, no crypto-origin funds, and no third-party aggregation; and (4) beneficiary-bank funds verification before treasury deployment. Because the RMI imposes no FX-approval requirement, the only flow-stoppers are OFAC/SDN screening at the U.S. correspondent and bank-level enhanced due diligence, both cleared by the beneficial-ownership extract, good-standing certificate, and W-8BEN-E or equivalent tax-beneficial-owner certification.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade disbursements settle through two complementary rails: (a) SWIFT MT103 customer transfers for escrow-to-vendor and operating payments, where the beneficiary bank, BIC, and account number are pre-validated and each message carries the invoice and purchase-order references; and (b) irrevocable commercial letters of credit under UCP 600, confirmed where the vendor is a first-time MRO or repair station, covering bulk rotables purchases with documents comprising commercial invoice, packing list, airway bill, FAA 8130-3 or EASA Form 1 or OEM release certificate, and the ECCN/EAR99 statement. The Escrow_Aviation rail is the primary settlement overlay for surplus transactions: the escrow agent holds funds against a Release-and-Pay Instruction, releasing only after successful part inspection and then passing a single MT103 to the vendor, eliminating counterparty non-performance risk. Before release, the bank-class compliance filter matches each disbursement against the consolidated SDN and restricted-parties lists; no physical cash or crypto settlement is permitted.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla deliverable FX forwards (EUR/USD, GBP/USD) matching invoice maturities, executed under a U.S. master-forward agreement with a Federal Reserve member bank and supported by completed-contract hedge documentation.

Cross-currency interest rate swaps (EUR/USD and GBP/USD) collateralized under a credit support annex, permissible where aircraft-parts payables are foreign-currency denominated and matched by identifiable trade liabilities.
Zero-premium FX collars on the principal surplus-corridor currencies (EUR, GBP, SGD) with upside capped at a pre-agreed strike, permissible as a trade-hedging overlay beyond pure spot.

Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in dollar-block Asian currencies (KRW, INR, TWD, CNH) executed through a U.S.-licensed or EU-licensed dealer, permissible because the RMI imposes no currency-use or derivative-licensing restriction on a tax-exempt non-resident entity, subject to counterparty credit approval.

FX spot conversion for same-day settlement of multi-currency trade payables; deliverable-only, with exotic options, barrier options, and digital structures excluded to avoid suitability and documentation objections.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Report (Form ACR) — directors, officers, share capital, registered office/agent confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Republic of the Marshall Islands (filed through the licensed resident registered agent)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 30 April of each calendar year; reporting period covers the preceding calendar year ending 31 December
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of USD 100 or 10% of the due fee (whichever is greater), plus monthly late penalty of USD 50; two consecutive missed annual reports place the corporation on the inactive register and permit administrative strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Franchise Tax Return and Payment (based on authorized share structure)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Corporations and RMI Treasury (remitted through the licensed resident registered agent)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due on or before 30 April of each calendar year; no extensions available; newly incorporated entities pay a pro-rated franchise tax for the incorporation year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Interest accrues at 1.5% per month or fraction of a month on unpaid tax; continued delinquency results in loss of good standing; three consecutive unpaid years authorize the Registrar to dissolve administratively and disclaim the corporate name

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Registered Office and Registered Agent Renewal — continuous statutory requirement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Licensed resident registered agent; notification filed with the Registrar upon any resignation or change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Maintained on a continuous basis; the 30 April annual corporate report confirms the current registered office and agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain a registered office and agent for 30 days permits the Registrar to issue a notice of deficiency; if unresolved for a further 60 days, administrative dissolution may proceed

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership (UBO) Register Confirmation — in-house statutory record retained at the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Licensed resident registered agent as the designated AML responsible person; produced to the RMI Financial Intelligence Unit upon lawful request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Updated within 15 days after any UBO change or share transfer; annual confirmation executed concurrently with the 30 April corporate report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-maintenance of current UBO records may attract a monetary penalty of up to USD 1,000 per violation under RMI AML regulations, trigger registered-agent resignation, and create adverse due-diligence findings for aviation escrow and Swift-wire banking partners

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No RMI statutory audit requirement applies to a non-resident Business Corporation engaged in surplus aircraft parts distribution solely on a non-domestic basis. A mandatory independent audit is triggered only where the entity is licensed under RMI banking, insurance, or trust-industry legislation, or where shareholders holding at least 25% of issued voting shares demand an audit. No revenue or asset threshold in the RMI Business Corporations Act creates a general annual audit duty for exempt non-resident business corporations.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: RMI law does not prescribe a single domestic accounting framework for non-resident exempt corporations; books and records must be sufficient to enable full financial disclosure. IFRS is the customary framework for cross-border aviation rotables inventory and spares trading, and is acceptable where consistently adopted by the Board. Other internationally recognized GAAP, including US GAAP, may also be used where required by an aircraft-parts certification body or a financing bank.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Marshall Islands has no public UBO filing with the Registrar. The Business Corporation must maintain a current beneficial ownership register at its registered office. Upon any share transfer, the instrument of transfer is lodged with the registered agent and the Register of Members is updated within 15 days. The registered agent performs an annual confirmation of UBO data as part of the 30 April corporate report and must present the record to the RMI Financial Intelligence Unit upon lawful request. No separate government UBO annual return is filed.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US $400 – $800 through a licensed Marshall Islands registered agent (includes registered office, registered agent, UBO record maintenance, and preparation of the annual report)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US $1,500 – $4,500 if a voluntary independent audit is obtained; audit is not statutorily required for the non-resident aviation spares trading Business Corporation

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% (non-resident Business Corporation wholly exempt; RMI Income Tax Act taxes only income sourced within the Republic)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory offshore exemption; annual fixed franchise tax of USD 200 to USD 2,500 depending on authorized share tier; no capital gains tax, no gross receipts tax, no branch remittance tax, no payroll tax exposure where no RMI payroll; NOL mechanism not applicable to exempt offshore entities

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: RMI Annual Report (Form AR) filed under Section 94 of the Business Corporations Act 1990 (as amended); submitted through the licensed Registered Agent to the Registrar of Corporations, Ministry of Finance, Majuro. No separate corporate income tax return exists for exempt non-resident BCs; the Annual Report is the sole statutory filing. The Registrar does not operate a mandatory public e-filing portal; submissions are paper-based or agent-transmitted.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: On or before the last day of the month in which the anniversary of incorporation falls (e.g., incorporation on 15 March, due by 31 March); no pro-rated or partial-year cycle is available

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exact corporate name and registration number as recorded in the BCCA registry
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the registered corporate name including suffix 'Corporation' or 'Inc.'; no trade-name translation or alternative style is permitted

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered office in the Republic and full identity of the licensed Registered Agent
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the agent's RMI address (e.g., Trust Company Complex, Majuro); the non-resident cannot designate a PO Box as the registered office and must retain an RMI-licensed agent

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Authorized capital: number of shares and par value per class
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For no-par shares state 'no par value'; this field determines the USD 200 to USD 2,500 franchise tax tier and must not be understated

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Issued and outstanding shares with consideration paid
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Certify that shares are held by non-residents; RMI citizenship or residence is not required

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Directors and officers: full legal names, nationality, residential addresses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident directors are permitted; nominee directors must disclose beneficial owners in the confidential beneficial ownership declaration attached to the Annual Report

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Principal business address outside the Republic and description of commercial activity
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the operational headquarters address and describe 'wholesale distribution of certified civil aircraft rotables and avionics surplus' (ISIC 4659 / NAICS 423860); explicitly declare that no trade is conducted from and no gross income is sourced in the Republic

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of offshore status and absence of RMI-source income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Execute the prescribed declaration confirming the entity has no RMI business, no RMI assets other than the registered office, and no RMI-source receipts; this declaration underpins the income tax exemption and must be truthful

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Signature of officer or director and certification date
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must be executed by a natural person; electronic signatures accepted only where authorized by the Registered Agent under the RMI Electronic Transactions Act

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Economic substance declaration: relevant activity and core income-generating activities performed in the Republic
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify the distribution and service center activity under ISIC 4659; state the number of RMI employees, the local premises address, and annual local operating expenditure; due concurrently with the Annual Report

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing surcharge of USD 500 per default; failure for two consecutive filing cycles exposes the corporation to summary administrative dissolution by the Registrar without judicial order; reinstatement requires payment of all franchise tax arrears, penalties, reinstatement fees and re-certification of a licensed Registered Agent; false filings additionally trigger criminal misdemeanor liability

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% on dividends declared from non-RMI-source profits; a 3% final statutory withholding tax applies only where a dividend is deemed derived from sources within the Republic under the Income Tax Act
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The Republic of the Marshall Islands has not concluded any comprehensive double taxation agreement (DTA); only Tax Information Exchange Agreements (TIEAs) exist. Treaty relief is therefore unavailable. Relief is obtained domestically: the exempt BC relies on the statutory exemption and obtains from the Registrar a Certificate of Good Standing together with a Tax Exemption / Non-Resident Status Certificate, submitted to foreign payors and tax authorities as proof that the RMI levied no income tax on the entity. Because RMI withholds nothing, no foreign tax credit arises at the RMI level.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory RMI-source rate: 3% final withholding tax on interest, royalties and rents sourced within the Republic, payable by the RMI remitter; offshore flows: 0% withholding by the BC; no treaty reductions available (no DTA) and no special interest/royalty exemption regime

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: None prescribed. RMI maintains no Local File, Master File or Country-by-Country reporting regime, and the Income Tax Act does not impose transfer-pricing adjustments on exempt offshore entities. However, Economic Substance Regulations compliance requires the BC to retain contemporaneous evidence that intercompany remuneration paid to RMI-office personnel and related suppliers is consistent with the OECD arm's-length principle, including a functional and cost analysis of purchasing, inventory, pricing and risk functions performed in the Republic.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Economic Substance Regulations 2020 (as amended) apply to every Business Corporation carrying on a Relevant Activity under the BCCA. For a distribution and service center, the Core Income-Generating Activities — procurement of certified aircraft rotables and avionics surplus, inventory holding and management, pricing decisions, supply-chain risk assumption, and sales/distribution coordination — must be directed and managed in the Republic, with adequate physical premises, full-time employees and local operating expenditure proportionate to the trading profile. The pure equity-holding entity exemption does not apply to ISIC 4659 trading activity. Annual ESR returns are due concurrently with the Annual Report; failure to demonstrate substance triggers penalty action by the Registrar.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and False Corporate Disclosure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly under-declaring authorized share capital in the Annual Report to remain in a lower USD 200 to USD 300 franchise fee tier; submitting a false offshore-status declaration while generating RMI-source sales of aircraft parts; engineering transactions to conceal beneficial ownership of diverted surplus inventory
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal misdemeanor penalties under the BCCA including fines and imprisonment; administrative reassessment of the correct franchise tax tier with mandatory payment of all shortfalls; disqualification of the Registered Agent if knowingly involved; publication of the enforcement action by the RMI Companies Office
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who signed or authorized the false Annual Report or offshore declaration are jointly and severally liable for unpaid franchise taxes, statutory penalties and prosecution costs; criminal conviction may carry imprisonment; court-issued travel restrictions may be imposed pending investigation or restitution under RMI criminal procedure

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the surplus aircraft-parts distribution business with no physical office in the Republic, no locally engaged employees, all board and strategic decisions taken offshore, and failure to file the annual Economic Substance Return; use of nominee directors and undisclosed trust shareholdings to simulate local presence
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Financial penalties up to USD 20,000 for non-compliance, rising on repeat default; cancellation of the economic substance certificate; administrative strike-off of the corporation; cross-border re-characterization by foreign tax authorities as managed and controlled in their jurisdiction, exposing the full foreign corporate income tax on the aircraft-parts margins plus penalties
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be disqualified from acting as directors of any RMI corporation; fines may be enforced personally where the entity cannot pay; deliberate concealment of substance failures is prosecuted as fraud; travel bans can be ordered where directors fail to cooperate with the Registrar or the Financial Intelligence Unit

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML/CTF Breach in Aviation Spares Payment Rails
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting escrow/SWIFT transfers from sanctioned or high-risk aviation counterparties; processing cash or third-party payments for surplus certificated parts without beneficial-owner due diligence; structuring settlements to avoid the RMI suspicious-transaction reporting threshold; failing to maintain AML policies and a designated compliance officer for the trading activity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Offences under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism Act and the RMI Criminal Code: fines up to USD 100,000 per count, forfeiture of the aircraft-part inventory and proceeds, mandatory FIU reporting orders, and suspension or revocation of the corporate registration
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers are criminally liable for willful blindness and may be sentenced to imprisonment; personal civil restitution to defrauded counterparties is recoverable through veil-piercing where corporate funds are used for illegal escrow diversion; travel bans and asset freezes are standard FIU and court measures pending resolution

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlicensed RMI Domestic Activity and Foreign Investment License Evasion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the non-resident BC as a de facto trading platform with RMI customers, maintaining warehouse operations in Majuro, or invoicing RMI-based airlines and MRO providers for aircraft parts without a Foreign Investment Business License and the associated Business Licence, thereby converting exempt offshore status into a taxable RMI permanent establishment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Suspension or cancellation of the BC registration; ministerial fines for each unlicensed transaction; confiscation of profits derived from RMI-source sales; application of the 3% statutory withholding and domestic assessment on RMI-source gross income under the Income Tax Act
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who directed the unlicensed local sales are personally liable for business license fees, fines and any tax assessment; civil veil-piercing is available to RMI counterparties injured by the unlawful trading; in egregious cases, directors face imprisonment and court-administered travel bans pending satisfaction of monetary judgments

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlawful Distribution and Reckless Dividend Stripping
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Declaring dividends to non-resident shareholders while the corporation is insolvent or after repaying related-party loans ahead of trade creditors; distributing surplus aircraft-parts proceeds without a solvency certification; disguising shareholder loans as dividends to avoid the 3% RMI-source withholding where applicable
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Unlawful distribution provisions of the BCCA: the distribution is voidable to the extent it impairs capital; the corporation must restore the amounts with interest; the Registrar may dissolve the corporation if solvency cannot be re-established; foreign creditors may enforce against the RMI assets
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who voted for or authorized the unlawful distribution are jointly and severally liable to restore the full amount with interest; piercing the corporate veil permits creditors to bring personal civil suits; serious cases involving fraudulent conveyance result in criminal sanctions, travel bans and imprisonment
